newsitem.title: USA: DC officials pleased with $229.3 mln bond sale.
newsitem.headline: DC officials pleased with $229.3 mln bond sale.

text.p: District of Columbia officials said they are pleased with the results of Wednesday's sale of $229.3 million in general obligation bonds to Lehman Brothers at a 6.0734 percent interest rate.

"The results of this sale compare favorably to the results of the District's October 1996 sale of GO bonds and indicates that the pricing of the District's debt obligations has improved in the last eight months," DC Chief Financial Officer Anthony Williams said in a statement.
"Today reflects the growing confidence the investment community has in the District's financial recovery," Williams added.
Williams said that in October, 1996, DC bonds yielded 105 to 170 basis points higher than insured triple A rated bonds.
By contrast, in Wednesday's sale city bonds yielded 15 to 65 basis points higher than insured triple A rated bonds, an improvement of 90 to 105 basis points over the October sale, Williams said.
Closing is expected June 4 on the bonds, which carry a Ba2 rating from Moody's Investors Service, B from Standard & Poor's Corporation, and BB from Fitch Investor Service.
About $150 million of bond proceeds will go toward funding capital improvements to schools, streets, fire department equipment and other facilities.
